page.title: Approve the design of Example app
page.lede: Example app lets people report place conditions and read the latest report for a place before they go.

sections.title: Claude's evaluation
sections.hint: The design against the rules, before you read it

items.text: Every requirement has a design part that answers it
Every decision names what was rejected
Every target has a check that can fail
Offline use is designed end to end

rows.title: Offline reports are queued on the phone, but the sync rule for two reports on one place is not decided.
rows.label: high

body.text: A person with no signal files a report. Another files one for the same place an hour later with a signal. Which one is shown first is not yet decided.

items: Newest report wins (simple, but loses the first person's detail).
Both are shown, newest on top (more to read).

rows.title: Reports are plain records with a place, a time and a condition from a fixed list.
rows.label: medium

body.text: The condition list is: clear, wet, muddy, snow, blocked. Free text is kept as a note.

body.label: Rejected
body.text: Free-text reports: they cannot be filtered or compared.

rows.title: Accounts are optional: a person can report with only a nickname.
rows.label: high
rows.round_note: You asked for fewer sign-in steps, so a nickname is enough to report.

body.text: A nickname is stored with each report. A nickname is not an identity, so edits and deletes are only possible within the hour after filing, from the same phone.

body.label: Round 1
body.text: Every report needed an account with an e-mail address.

rows.title: Place data comes from a public map source and is refreshed once a week.
rows.label: low

body.text: The source's licence allows reuse with credit. The credit is shown on the place page.

rows.title: Reports filed without signal wait in a queue on the phone and are sent when it is back online.
rows.label: critical
rows.round_note: Added after you asked what happens on a place with no signal.

body.text: The queue holds up to 50 reports and keeps the time the report was filed, not the time it was sent.

head: Case
What happens
rows: Oldest report is kept, newest is refused with a message
Queue is lost; the form warns before this

rows.title: Photos are not part of version 1.
rows.label: low
rows.round_note: Dropped to keep the first version small.

body.text: Photos need storage, size limits and review of what is shown. They return as their own change.

rows.title: The server keeps the last 90 days of reports and removes older ones each night.
rows.label: medium
rows.round_note: The window was 30 days; you asked for 90 so that seasonal places keep their history.

body.text: Removal is a nightly job and is logged. Reports older than 90 days are not recoverable.

body.label: Round 1
body.text: The server keeps the last 30 days of reports.

sections.title: Threats
sections.hint: Ordered by how costly each is to get wrong

rows.title: Someone reports a blocked place that is open.
rows.label: high

body.text: A report older than 7 days is shown as old. Three recent reports outweigh one.

rows.title: A script files thousands of fake reports.
rows.label: critical

body.text: Reports are limited per phone and per network address. The limit is checked by the server, not the app.
A short blocklist is checked when the nickname is saved.
The last good copy of place data is kept and used.
